actuation: Positive-pressure pneumatic actuation (segmented spherical Dragon Skin 30 airbag regulated via electro-pneumatic proportional valves)
Rod-driven actuation (four circumferentially arranged Nitinol rods driven by stepper motors and linear lead screws; one base lead-screw slide)
constitutive_assumptions: Airbag acts primarily as a quasi-hydrostatic pressure transmission medium beyond an initial threshold (>12.5 kPa), transmitting normal contact pressure uniformly across jamming surfaces toward the sphere center in accordance with Pascal's Principle
Coulomb friction model governs interfacial locking torque between interleaved rigid jamming layers with a constant friction coefficient
Infinitesimal displacements / small deformations occur between jamming layers during the stiffness generation process
Equivalence between external mechanical work and friction torque dissipation based on the principle of virtual work
Piecewise constant curvature (PCC) assumption: each bending segment maintains an incompressible circular arc of uniform curvature
Mass of the actuation alloy rods is negligible relative to the continuum segment mass
control_variables: Airbag wall thickness optimized to 1.5 mm (Dragon Skin 30 silicone)
Jamming layer configuration fixed to 3 layers (dual-layer upper interface, triple-layer lower interface)
Feed rate of lead-screw testbed set to 5 mm/s for quasi-static stiffness evaluation
Cyclic motion parameters: 10 mm amplitude at 1 mm/s for hysteresis loops
Locking air pressure maintained at 250 kPa during obstacle avoidance and manipulation experiments
Base linear translation speed set to 5 mm/s during manipulation
Fabrication temperatures: wax injection and melting both conducted at 100 °C
dependent_variables: Stiffness switching times (seconds for stiff-to-compliant and compliant-to-stiff transitions)
Dissipated energy per cycle (Ediss) and equivalent damping ratio (ζeq)
Kinematic positioning error (average and maximum deviations in mm and percentage of length)
Surface wear and stiffness degradation over cyclic loading

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The multi-layer jamming spherical joint achieves a maximum stiffness of 1403.03 N/m at 300 kPa and a stiffness modulation ratio of 35.85 relative to 12.5 kPa with isotropic planar response.
Stiffness switching times between compliant and stiff states range from 0.07 s to 0.43 s, with exhaust rate becoming constrained by valve orifice dimensions above 50 kPa.
Segmented underactuation achieves four-segment motion using only four embedded Nitinol rods by sequentially switching segmental stiffness states, reducing required drive motors by 75%.
Sequential stiffness modulation introduces an estimated cumulative pneumatic latency of approximately 3.44 s across four segments during multi-segment reconfiguration.
Piecewise constant curvature kinematic modeling yields an average tip positioning error of 1.38 mm (1.15% length) for a single segment and 15.1 mm (3.2% length) for four segments.
Under cyclic reciprocating bending at 75 kPa, the joint exhibits a 3.6% (89 N/m) loss in secant stiffness after 1000 cycles due to interfacial friction wear.
Pressure endurance tests identify seal failure between the silicone airbag and the rigid base as the primary operational constraint, capping operating pressure at 300 kPa.
The equivalent damping ratio decreases from approximately 0.05 to 0.015 as pressure increases from 0 to 300 kPa, with peak energy dissipation occurring near 75 kPa.
The four-segment continuum arm mounted with a commercial pneumatic soft gripper successfully navigated a 3D constrained corridor with vertical obstacles to retrieve a 50 g object.

experimental_setup: Stiffness characterization testbed: 138 g continuum segment mounted horizontally, connected via tensile cord to a digital force gauge on a lead-screw stage (5 mm/s feed rate) regulated by electro-pneumatic proportional valves (ITV1030-312BL)
Pressure endurance apparatus measuring internal pressure and identifying seal leakage thresholds up to and exceeding 300 kPa
Dynamic transition setup recording force-time profiles during stepper-motor-induced displacement and controlled inflation/deflation
Cyclic hysteresis setup: segment actuated by four Nitinol rods with bidirectional push-pull motion (10 mm amplitude, 1 mm/s) driven by rigid links with revolute joints

Cyclic durability testbed: reciprocating bending (+90° to -90°) at 75 kPa over 1000 cycles, evaluating secant stiffness at 200 kPa every 100 cycles and inspecting surface morphology via digital microscope (Z01-4)
Kinematic validation testbed: Tracker motion capture tracking segment end-effectors in the XOZ plane at 10° increments (single segment) and 30° increments (four segments) up to 90°

Constrained manipulation setup: narrow corridor marked with simulated boundary walls and rigid vertical obstacle poles, base linear slide (R-5), four driving rods (R-1 to R-4), and distal commercial soft gripper (BMC-22219) picking a 50 g weight at 250 kPa joint locking pressure
future_work: Developing advanced hybrid control algorithms to bridge the gap toward continuous decoupling and enhance motion accuracy
Addressing manufacturing precision for miniaturization in medical intervention applications
Optimizing the strength-to-weight ratio to support structural upscaling for heavy-duty industrial inspections
Incorporating identified damping and hysteresis parameters into dynamic modeling and controller tuning
independent_variables: Actuation airbag pressure (varying between 0 kPa and 300 kPa)
Bending angle and deflection angle (angular range 0° to 90°)
Bending plane orientation (0°, 45°, and 90° azimuth angles)
Number of continuous bending cycles (up to 1000 cycles)
Segment configuration (single segment vs. four-segment series)
Segment operational state (locked vs. unlocked; sequential switching order)
Nitinol rod displacements and base slide translation
limitations_inferred: Stiffness, hysteresis, and durability characterizations were conducted solely in 2D planar bending, leaving out-of-plane torsional stiffness and multi-axial coupled loads unmeasured
Maximum payload capacity of 2 kg was demonstrated only on an isolated single segment, whereas the four-segment arm was demonstrated with a 50 g payload
The multi-step lost-wax casting process and SLA 3D printing of thin nested spherical shells require manual hole sealing and assembly, which may challenge manufacturing repeatability and scalability
Sequential 'unlock-actuate-lock' underactuation requires holding non-active segments in fixed rigid postures, precluding continuous simultaneous whole-arm dynamic maneuvers
limitations_stated_by_authors: Sequential underactuation introduces cumulative pneumatic switching latency (approximately 3.44 s across four segments), prolonging total execution time compared to simultaneous actuation
Above 50 kPa, exhaust rate is restricted by the proportional valve exhaust orifice size, making deflation slower than inflation
Operating pressures exceeding 300 kPa compromise the mechanical seal between the silicone airbag and rigid base, resulting in pneumatic leakage

Positioning error increases with bending angle and segment count due to axial compression of silicone airbags, irregular inter-layer squeezing friction at high curvatures, cumulative geometric deviations, and gravity-induced sagging
Friction-induced surface wear between jamming layers occurs during repeated motion and high-pressure locking, causing a 3.6% reduction in stiffness over 1000 cycles
The sequential mode differs from fully actuated continuum robots by lacking continuous motion decoupling
main_results: Stiffness of a single segment increased from 39.14 N/m at 12.5 kPa to 1403.03 N/m at 300 kPa, achieving a 35.85-fold modulation ratio with isotropic performance across three bending directions
Stiffness switching times ranged between 0.07 s and 0.43 s for individual transitions across the tested pressure range
The underactuated design reduced the number of driving motors by 75% (from 16 to 4 motors) while maintaining multi-segment shape control
A single segment achieved a maximum payload capacity of 2 kg
Kinematic positioning errors averaged 1.38 mm (1.15% length, max 3.24 mm) for a single segment and 15.1 mm (3.2% length, max 28 mm) for the four-segment robot
Durability testing showed an 89 N/m (3.6%) stiffness loss after 1000 reciprocating bending cycles at 75 kPa
The four-segment arm demonstrated 3D obstacle avoidance and payload retrieval of a 50 g mass within a confined corridor under 250 kPa locking pressure
modeling_methods: Interfacial friction locking torque formulation based on Coulomb friction integrated over spherical micro-elements
Structural stiffness prediction derived via the principle of virtual work under small-deformation assumptions
Piecewise constant curvature (PCC) forward kinematics mapping actuator rod lengths to configuration space (bending and deflection angles) and Cartesian task space
Energy method formulation to quantify dissipated energy and equivalent damping ratio (ζeq) from cyclic hysteresis loops
MATLAB numerical workspace simulation establishing an ellipsoidal reachable boundary (870 mm × 870 mm × 716 mm)
performance_metrics: Maximum structural stiffness (1403.03 N/m at 300 kPa)
Minimum structural stiffness (39.14 N/m at 12.5 kPa)
Individual stiffness switching duration (0.07 s to 0.43 s)
Cumulative pneumatic switching latency (approx. 3.44 s for four segments)
Manipulation target payload (50 g grasped using a 48.3 g soft gripper)
Average and maximum positioning errors (single segment: 1.38 mm / 3.24 mm; four segments: 15.1 mm / 28 mm)
Maximum safe operational pressure limit (300 kPa)
Stiffness degradation rate under cyclic wear (3.6% after 1000 cycles)
Equivalent damping ratio range (0.05 down to 0.015)
possible_gap_implications: While underactuation achieves a 75% reduction in motor count, the resulting sequential cumulative switching latency highlights an inherent trade-off between drive system simplicity and dynamic reconfiguration speed in variable-stiffness continuum robots

Positive-pressure layer jamming overcomes the 1-atmosphere vacuum limitation, but contact wear at elevated operating pressures indicates that long-term tribological stability remains a critical factor for frictional locking mechanisms

Discrepancies between constant-curvature kinematic predictions and experimental trajectories under large deflections underline the necessity of incorporating gravity sagging, axial compression, and inter-layer friction into high-curvature continuum robot modeling
paper.research_objective: To design, fabricate, model, and experimentally characterize an underactuated variable-stiffness continuum robot utilizing multi-layer jamming spherical joints (MLJSJs) actuated by positive-pressure internal airbags, enabling wide-range stiffness tuning and sequential multi-segment control using only four actuation rods.
paper.research_problem: Continuum robots commonly suffer from insufficient stiffness, which impairs motion controllability and load capacity, while conventional cable-driven multi-segment continuum robots face actuation redundancy and internal routing congestion caused by requiring separate sets of cables for each segment.
stiffness_mechanism: frictional locking between interleaved resin layers
paper.title: An Underactuated Variable Stiffness Continuum Robot With Multi-Layer Jamming Spherical Joints
